name: PointCast atlas
description: Every court, spot, shrine, paddle, league, page, agent and tool PointCast knows how to place, in one file. The 25-mile El Segundo layer first, then wider.
licenseNote: Records carry their own license when it differs; OpenStreetMap-derived records are ODbL-1.0 with attribution.
notOfficial: PointCast is an independent project. Not an official City of El Segundo page.

layers.name: Courts
layers.description: South Bay public pickleball courts from the PointCast Air desk: where they are, what they cost, how to get on.
layers.notes: Facts and dates come from src/data/courts-schedule.json; each fact cites a public page. Facts credited only to the desk (not a public page) are left out. Coordinates exist only where the elsegundo.xyz pickleball venue register matches by address; other courts carry no location.

layers.name: Pickleball
layers.description: The Pickleball Home page. The Squeeze team desk is held back until a public source exists.
layers.notes: The Squeeze league desk is omitted: its facts are transcribed from league-app screenshots with no public PTL page, it carries a DUPR figure, and the desk names people. It can be added as a league record once Mike approves a first-party exception in ATLAS.md §5. No rosters or player names anywhere.

layers.name: Paddle Register
layers.description: Pickleball paddle lines with launch dates, builds, list prices, approval status and public source links.
layers.notes: One gear record per paddle in the register (92 paddles at build time; the exact count is in counts.byLayer.paddles). Launch dates are on-sale or store-listing dates, not review dates. Gear has no location. "approved" means the register lists the paddle as USA Pickleball approved; "delisted" means the register logged a delisting with no later approval.

layers.name: Quiet places, weather stations and sky feeds
layers.description: Small Shrines (five one-minute pauses), the NOAA stations the weather atlas and the Tide shrine read, and the sun, moon, Pacific and air guide feeds.
layers.notes: Shrines come from src/data/small-shrines.ts and are dated by public/images/small-shrines/provenance.json. Stations come from src/data/weather-atlas.json (NOAA coordinates as published there, dated 2026-10-02); the Santa Monica tide station 9410840 takes its coordinates from public/pacific.json (reviewed 2026-10-06). Feeds are dated by their own reviewed field. Shrine-crawl, Elemental Shrine, Shrine of the Open Road, Ten Doors and Sitting with Gandalf are not emitted: none carries a dated, citable provenance. The morning-*.json manifests and the Desk house agents are not feeds of an upstream provider and are left out.

layers.name: Atlases and manufacturers
layers.description: PointCast research atlases as dataset records, and the 23 South Bay manufacturers from the manufacturing atlas.
layers.notes: Manufacturing records come from src/data/manufacturing-atlas.json (checkedDate 2026-10-02). That dataset intentionally has null coordinates, so these businesses carry no location; each cites the organization's own public pages, which show advertised capability, not audited capacity. The blocks atlas is derived from the blocks feed (generatedAt 2026-07-19). The Home Cartography demo is fictional; its check date 2026-10-06 is the last commit date of its feed file, as the data carries no as-of field. No store-level cannabis data is here.

layers.name: Dispensary Atlas (reference)
layers.description: Pointer to the research atlas of licensed cannabis retailers within 25 miles of El Segundo. The stores are not inlined.
layers.notes: Cannabis material: every record in this layer carries sensitive: ["cannabis"] so sister sites and map filters can drop it. One dataset record only; the 485 licensed retailers (46 microbusinesses are excluded by the dataset) are read from /dispensary-atlas.json, not copied into the atlas.

layers.name: Areas, radio plan and UES
layers.description: The 19 South Bay towns PointCast plans around, the seven planned radio stations, University of El Segundo classes, and the local-area program pages.
layers.notes: Area records carry no coordinates: the beacon list in src/lib/neighborhoods.ts states only a rounded distance and a compass bearing, which would put different towns on the same point, so they list and filter by area until a sourced representative point (Census place or GNIS) is added (NEXT-20-LAYERS layer 17). The neighborhoods file carries no as-of date, so 2026-10-06 is its last commit date. UES and local-area pages use the same commit date (2026-10-06) because those files carry no as-of field. Radio stations are a plan: nothing is on air. UES-104 and UES-207 mention cannabis education and carry sensitive: ["cannabis"].

layers.name: Agents
layers.description: The agents that work on PointCast: residents, the Desk's house agents, and the fictional Nouns characters of the Grok field.
layers.notes: Residents come from src/data/residents.ts (listed in /agents.json); their checked date is the mint date in src/data/agent-identities.json (per instance where one exists, else the file date). Open slots are planned records. House agents come from AIR_DESK in src/lib/air.ts and the Grok roster from src/data/grok-roster.json; neither has an as-of field, so their date is the last commit date of the source file (2026-10-06) and their source is the page that shows them. Public keys, hosts and machine names in agent-identities.json are deliberately not read. The Desk callers (Sol, Terra, Luna, Frog) are not separate records.

layers.name: MCP tools
layers.description: Every tool the PointCast MCP server offers to agents, with whether it only reads or can also write.
layers.notes: Built from tools/list on functions/api/mcp.ts. checked and updated are the day the list was last reviewed against mcp.ts (CATALOGUE_REVIEWED); tests/atlas-tools-layer.test.mjs fails when the tool names drift. "read-only" follows the server's own readOnlyHint annotation; a tool marked write can post, append, tap, play, set, ask, submit, offer or claim.

layers.name: Surfaces and feeds
layers.description: Pages and feeds PointCast lists as its current doors for agents, plus one feed per channel.
layers.notes: One record per concrete URL in AGENT_SURFACES (human, json, api, feeds). The registry has no as-of field, so the date is the last commit date of src/data/agent-surfaces.ts (2026-10-25). URL templates with {id}, {handle}, {date} or {name} are patterns, not places, and are left out. The Pickleball Home page is recorded by the pickleball layer, not here. Channel feeds come from CHANNEL_LIST in src/lib/channels.ts (file date 2026-10-06) and the /c/[channel].json route.

layers.name: Block archive
layers.description: The PointCast block archive: numbered posts across ten channels, with a JSON feed and an MCP reader.
layers.notes: The 500+ blocks are referenced through https://pointcast.xyz/blocks.json and the blocks_search / block_read MCP tools, not inlined, so this layer holds one dataset record. count is the number of files in src/content/blocks at build time; updated is the newest block timestamp.

layers.name: Outdoors (OPEN/25)
layers.description: Public parks, beaches, courts, gardens and preserves from the PointCast OPEN/25 open-air field guide, each linked to the official page that describes it.
layers.notes: Facts come from OUTDOOR_RESOURCES in src/lib/radius25-outdoors.ts (25 resources). The module carries one edition date (OPEN_AIR_COMMONS.updatedAt, 2026-08-02) and no per-resource dates, so every record uses that date as checked/updated. Coordinates exist only where the elsegundo.xyz curated places register (or architecture catalog, non-estimated points) holds the same place; other resources carry no location.

layers.name: Geology field walks
layers.description: Four slow field walks from the University of El Segundo geology track: where to stand and what to read in the ground.
layers.notes: FIELD_WALKS in src/lib/geology.ts cite no per-walk public sources (CITATIONS list publishers without URLs, and the module has no as-of date), so each record is labeled derived from the geology.json twin and uses the git date of src/lib/geology.ts (2026-10-06) as checked/updated. The route /geology has no human page in src/pages, so url points at the JSON twin. A walk is located only when its place text contains the name of a located place in the committed elsegundo.xyz atlas snapshot.

layers.name: Taprooms
layers.description: Southern California breweries on the PointCast Taproom carry list, each linked to its own website.
layers.notes: Names, neighborhoods and founding years come from src/data/taproom.json (_lastReviewed 2026-04-24). Each record cites the brewery's own website. Vibe copy and beer lists stay on the page. Coordinates come from the committed elsegundo.xyz atlas snapshot only when exactly one located business there has the same name; the position keeps that record's precision, source and license.

layers.name: Real-estate market lenses
layers.description: The place lenses of the PointCast 25-mile real-estate study: one anchor per city or district, with the public planning sources behind it.
layers.notes: From localMarkets in src/lib/real-estate-local.mjs (checked 2026-10-03). Only the Main Street lens carries a coordinate (Census-geocoded City Hall point); the other anchors are editorial and unsourced, so they are listed without a location. Each lens point in the study is an approximate editorial study anchor: the module states that no neighborhood, city, parcel or listing boundary is implied, so location precision is city. The module gives no coordinate source for most anchors; the source on each location is the lens's first cited public source, and only the El Segundo Main Street anchor is the Census-geocoded City Hall point. Not a legal boundary.

records.name: Abalone Cove Park / Reserve
records.summary: Abalone Cove Park / Reserve, Rancho Palos Verdes: bluff · trails · marine reserve edge. A check-first coastal geology and tide-edge room: bluff views, bounded trail movement, no-take attention, and a leave-it-there practice.

records.name: Baldwin Hills Scenic Overlook
records.summary: Baldwin Hills Scenic Overlook, Culver City: steep trail · stairs · native habitat · view. A vertical day marker: choose stairs or trail honestly, stop before strain, read the restored landscape, and make the horizon the finish line.

records.name: Ballona Creek Bike Path
records.summary: Ballona Creek Bike Path, Culver City to coast: separated linear path · creek channel. A continuous-line day: choose a bounded out-and-back, make three observation stops, and let the path—not a destination—be the game.

records.name: Bruce's Beach
records.summary: Bruce's Beach, Manhattan Beach: terraced grass · half court · ocean view. A short overlook room for one-ball HORSE variants, a history-and-art pause, a picnic, and a deliberate sunset finish.

source.label: fact
source.title: City of Manhattan Beach Parks & Facilities

records.name: Burton W. Chace Park
records.summary: Burton W. Chace Park, Marina del Rey: harbor point · lawn · pergolas. The marina living room: short laps, harbor drawing, chess or board-game tables, picnic shade, and a public-program handoff when scheduled.

records.name: Dockweiler State Beach
records.summary: Dockweiler State Beach, Playa del Rey: sand · bike path · pacific edge. The all-day coast door: bike-path motion, sand games, horizon work, volleyball, a picnic, and designated-fire-ring evenings when current conditions allow.

records.name: George F Canyon Preserve
records.summary: George F Canyon Preserve, Rolling Hills Estates: riparian canyon · coastal sage trail. A short habitat contrast: shaded canyon to sage, with one listening stop, one texture sketch, and nothing removed.

records.name: Hermosa Beach
records.summary: Hermosa Beach, Hermosa Beach: sand · strand · volleyball. A clean moving-social sequence: Strand walk, short mobility reset, beach-tennis or volleyball variation, then pier or horizon close.

records.name: Hopkins Wilderness Park
records.summary: Hopkins Wilderness Park, Redondo Beach: urban preserve · forest · meadow · pond. A small wilderness interval for a trail loop, quiet looking, kid-scale habitat comparison, and a no-collection observation card.

source.label: listing
source.title: City of Redondo Beach General Plan

records.name: Kenneth Hahn State Recreation Area
records.summary: Kenneth Hahn State Recreation Area, Los Angeles: regional parkland · trails · lawns · lake. A broad choose-your-own room for longer walking, field play, shade, family gathering, and a quiet transition between city and hill.

records.name: Library Park
records.summary: Library Park, El Segundo: old trees · open lawn · bandstand. A soft civic room for a reading blanket, drawing exchange, unamplified listening circle, or very slow group arrival.

source.label: fact
source.title: City of El Segundo Recreation & Parks

records.name: Madrona Marsh Preserve
records.summary: Madrona Marsh Preserve, Torrance: seasonal wetland · nature center · observation trail. A careful looking room: one slow circuit, bird and frog listening, field sketching, and a guided program only when actually scheduled.

records.name: Palisades Park
records.summary: Palisades Park, Santa Monica: clifftop path · lawns · public art · chess. A long, linear overlook for walking conversations, chess, public-art noticing, picnic intervals, and a close that does not require buying anything.

records.name: Polliwog Park
records.summary: Polliwog Park, Manhattan Beach: pond path · garden · lawn · amphitheater. A useful nature-and-neighborhood mix for bird minutes, garden color studies, StoryWalk pacing, picnics, and a low-key closing circle.

source.label: fact
source.title: City of Manhattan Beach Parks & Facilities

records.name: South Coast Botanic Garden
records.summary: South Coast Botanic Garden, Palos Verdes Peninsula: botanic paths · collections · shade. A paid public garden door for color study, plant-form drawing, a long easy walk, seasonal noticing, and a quiet bench close.

records.name: Tongva Park
records.summary: Tongva Park, Santa Monica: braided garden paths · overlooks · public art. The designed-landscape room: trace an arroyo line, compare plant textures, make a sculpture response on paper, then gather at the overlook.

records.name: Valley Park
records.summary: Valley Park, Hermosa Beach: basketball · play field · picnic grove. An inland counterweight to the sand: court games, field relays, a shaded reset, and an accessible family picnic base.

records.name: Read the sand layers
records.summary: A field walk at El Porto Beach at low tide: Look for heavy-mineral concentrations — the dark bands of magnetite and ilmenite the waves sort by density.

records.name: Stand on a Pleistocene dune
records.summary: A field walk at Imperial Avenue overlook, top of the dunes: You are standing on aeolian sand that arrived ~10,000 to 125,000 years ago.

records.name: Read the Palos Verdes uplift
records.summary: A field walk at Hilltop Park, looking south toward the peninsula: Each terrace on the peninsula is a former sea level, raised by tectonic uplift faster than the ocean could erode it.

records.name: See active sea-cliff retreat
records.summary: A field walk at Vista del Mar bluffs, walking south from Dockweiler: The bluff face is losing inches to feet per year.

records.name: White Point Nature Preserve
records.summary: White Point Nature Preserve, San Pedro: restored coastal sage · accessible trail · native garden. A long-view restoration room: accessible trail pacing, native-plant shapes, former-military landscape history, and a Catalina-facing close.

records.name: Garden shrine
records.summary: Nothing to hurry. Stay with one small thing that grows. A one-minute secular pause with artwork and optional synthesized sound.

records.name: Memory shrine
records.summary: Keep the small things. An ordinary detail can be worth keeping. A one-minute secular pause with artwork and optional synthesized sound.

records.name: Night shrine
records.summary: A light left on. You can leave a few things for tomorrow. A one-minute secular pause with artwork and optional synthesized sound.

records.name: Ocean shrine
records.summary: A little more room. Let the horizon hold the faraway things. A one-minute secular pause with artwork and optional synthesized sound.

records.name: Tide shrine
records.summary: The water comes back. The sea keeps its own time, twice a day. A one-minute secular pause with artwork and optional synthesized sound.
